questions.question: Identify the error in the given sentence: 'The new manager is very popular between his colleagues and subordinates.'

options.explanation: This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
The error lies here; 'between' should be replaced with 'among'.
This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.

questions.explanation: The preposition 'between' is used when referring to two people or things. When referring to more than two, 'among' should be used. Since there are 'colleagues and subordinates' (implying more than two), 'among' is the correct preposition.
questions.hint: Consider the number of entities involved in the comparison.
